Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :



Option 1) : ÷, -, +, ×, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 ÷ 17 - 54 + 18 × 6 = 56

⇒ 34 ÷ 17 - 54 + 18 × 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 54 + 18 × 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 54 + 108 = 56

⇒ 110 - 54 = 56

⇒ 56 = 56

LHS = RHS

Option 2) : ×, +, ÷, -, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 × 17 + 54 ÷ 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 × 17 + 54 ÷ 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 × 17 + 3 - 6 = 56

⇒ 578 + 3 - 6 = 56

⇒ 581 - 6 = 56

⇒ 575 ≠ 56

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : +, ÷, ×, -, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 + 17 ÷ 54 × 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 + 17 ÷ 54 × 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 + 0.314 × 18 - 6 = 56

⇒ 34 + 5.66 - 6 = 56

⇒ 39.66 - 6 = 56

⇒ 33.66 ≠ 56

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : ÷, -, ×, +, =

Given equation : 34 * 17 * 54 * 18 * 6 * 56

After inserting the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 34 ÷ 17 - 54 × 18 + 6 = 56

⇒ 34 ÷ 17 - 54 × 18 + 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 54 × 18 + 6 = 56

⇒ 2 - 972 + 6 = 56

⇒ 8 - 972 = 56

⇒ - 964 ≠ 56

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "÷, -, +, ×, =".

questions.q: The average score (runs/match) of Mithali before the start of the women's national series was 45. In the women's national series of 10 matches, her total score was 500 runs. Find the total number of matches played by her till date, if her new average after the series is 47.5.

The matches played before the start of the women's national series = x

The average score (runs/match) of Mithali before the start of the women's national series was 45 → 45x ........ (i)

In the women's national series of 10 matches, her total score was 500 runs → 500 ........ (ii)

The total number of matches played by her till date = x + 10

The total number of matches played by her till date, if her new average after the series is 47.5 → (x + 10) × 47.5 ......... (iii)

From equations (i), (ii) and (iii) we get,

⇒ 45x + 500 = (x + 10) × 47.5

⇒ 45x + 500 = 47.5x + 475

⇒ 2.5x = 25

⇒ x = 10

∴ The matches played before the start of the women's national series (x) = 10 matches.

∴ Here, The total number of matches played by her till date = x + 10

The total number of matches played by her till date = 10 + 10

The total number of matches played by her till date = 20

Hence, the correct answer is "20".

questions.q: Which of the following is commonly referred to as 'Ozone Hole'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Stratosphere.

Key Points

• An ozone hole refers to a region in the stratosphere where the concentration of ozone becomes extremely low in certain months.

• Ozone (chemically, a molecule of three oxygen atoms) is found mainly in the upper atmosphere, an area called the stratosphere, between 10 and 50 km from the earth's surface.

• The cause of the formation of the hole is attributed to the unusual weather at the poles.

• It is responsible for protecting life on Earth from the harmful UV radiation from the Sun.

• The lack of the Ozone layer can have severe implications for people living directly under it. The most prominent effects are Skin Cancer and other possibly fatal skin diseases.

Additional Information

Troposphere

It contains most of our weather - clouds, rain, snow. In this part of the atmosphere, the temperature gets colder as the distance above the earth increases, by about 6.5°C per km.

The troposphere contains about 75% of all of the air in the atmosphere, and almost all of the water vapour (which forms clouds and rain).

Biosphere

The biosphere is defined as the region on, above, and below the Earth’s surface where life exists.

The biosphere is related to the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere, which are all spheres of the physical world.

The lithosphere is the outermost layer of Earth, composed of the crust and the brittle part of the upper mantle.
